# Regime test results (generated by regime_test.py)

Diurnal-index rule: 0.5 deg Amazon cells with >= 200 Aqua+Terra daytime detections 2012-2020 (days both up); index = Aqua/Terra count ratio 2012-2020; terciles weighted by 2012-2020 Aqua detections. Cut points: A/T <= 2.425 (T1), <= 4.272 (T2), above (T3). Cells: 784.

Geographic rule: arc = latitude < -5 or longitude > -48; interior = rest of the Amazon biome.

## Interpretation (written by hand from the tables above; re-running the script overwrites this file)

- Prediction (Giglio 2007 regimes): later Aqua look -> L > 1 in the arc (peak ~15.6 h), L <= 1 in the interior rainforest (peak ~13.9 h).
- Geographic split: interior Aqua L (1.121 in 2024, 1.331 in 2025) is as high as or higher than arc (1.098, 1.262). Same sign, wrong order. Prediction not met.
- Diurnal-index terciles (2012-2020 Aqua/Terra): 2025 Aqua L = 1.172 (T1) / 1.510 (T2) / 1.283 (T3); 2024 = 1.088 / 1.099 / 1.139. No monotonic dose-response.
- Terra (09:12-09:19 in 2025) drops in every stratum (0.44-0.57 in 2025, except the 'sparse' cells), consistent with a morning ramp everywhere; in 2023-2024 T3 and interior Terra rose above 1, so Terra does not separate cleanly either.
- Caveats: Aqua/Terra index also carries the diurnal cloud cycle and the strength of the morning ramp, not only the peak time; the interior has the higher A/T (4.18 vs 2.48), the opposite of what Giglio's peak times imply, so the A/T index and the geographic labels may not map onto Giglio's regimes. 2023-2024 interior fires include the central-Amazon drought, which may change fire type. The reference ratio is held fixed in the bootstrap (intervals are too narrow by that much).
